pen.definition: A writing implement with a point from which ink flows.

pencil.definition: A writing tool with a thin core that makes marks on paper.

highlighter.definition: A bright pen used to mark important words.

marker.definition: A pen with a broad tip for writing or drawing.

eraser.definition: A tool used to remove pencil marks from paper.
eraser.exampleUsage: She used the eraser to remove the pencil mark.

mechanical-pencil.definition: A pencil that holds a thin replaceable lead and advances it through a mechanism rather than being sharpened.
mechanical-pencil.exampleUsage: The mechanical pencil uses 0.5 millimeter lead.

fountain-pen.definition: A pen that holds liquid ink and writes through a metal nib.
fountain-pen.exampleUsage: He filled the fountain pen with the specified ink.

felt-tip-pen.definition: A writing or drawing tool has a tip made from felt fibers and works on paper at home or school.
felt-tip-pen.exampleUsage: She wrote the heading with a felt-tip pen.

correction-tape.definition: A thin strip of opaque material rolled over printed or written text to cover a mistake.
correction-tape.exampleUsage: She used correction tape to cover the typing error.

whiteboard-marker.definition: A marker containing erasable ink designed for writing on whiteboards.
whiteboard-marker.exampleUsage: The teacher wrote the heading with a whiteboard marker.

paper.definition: A thin flat material used for writing or drawing.

notebook.definition: A book with blank pages for recording notes or memoranda.

legal-pad.definition: A pad of lined writing paper, traditionally yellow in the United States, often used for notes.
legal-pad.exampleUsage: He wrote meeting notes on a legal pad.

sticky-note.definition: A small piece of paper with a removable sticky back.

index-card.definition: A small card used for notes or study facts.

envelope.definition: A flat (usually rectangular) container for a letter, thin package, etc.

folder.definition: A cover used to hold and organize papers.

binder.definition: A thick cover with rings that holds loose pages.

manila-folder.definition: A paper file folder, traditionally made from light-brown manila card, used to organize documents.
manila-folder.exampleUsage: The documents were stored in a labeled manila folder.

label.definition: A small piece of paper or material used to identify an item.

stapler.definition: A tool that pushes metal staples through paper.
stapler.exampleUsage: The clerk joined the pages using a stapler.

paper-clip.definition: A small bent piece of metal used to hold papers.

binder-clip.definition: A spring-loaded metal clip with folding handles used to hold a stack of papers together.
binder-clip.exampleUsage: A binder clip held the pages together.

rubber-band.definition: A flexible loop used to hold things together.

pushpin.definition: A tack for attaching papers to a bulletin board or drawing board.

thumbtack.definition: A small pin used to attach paper to a board.

tape.definition: A strip of sticky material used to attach things.

glue-stick.definition: A small tube of glue used to join paper.

fastener.definition: A device that holds objects or papers together.

magnet.definition: (physics) a device that attracts iron and produces a magnetic field.
magnet.exampleUsage: A magnet held the paper against the metal board.

desk-organizer.definition: A tray, container, or stand designed to keep office supplies arranged on a desk.
desk-organizer.exampleUsage: Pens and notes were stored in the desk organizer.

pencil-cup.definition: A small upright container used to hold pens, pencils, and similar items.
pencil-cup.exampleUsage: The pencil cup contained pens and markers.

tape-dispenser.definition: A holder with a cutting edge used to store and dispense adhesive tape.
tape-dispenser.exampleUsage: The tape dispenser sat beside the stapler.

letter-tray.definition: A shallow tray used on a desk to hold documents, mail, or papers.
letter-tray.exampleUsage: Incoming papers were placed in the letter tray.

desk-lamp.definition: A small adjustable lamp designed to provide light over a desk or work surface.
desk-lamp.exampleUsage: The desk lamp illuminated the notebook.

mouse-pad.definition: A smooth surface that helps a computer mouse move accurately.

wrist-rest.definition: A padded support placed in front of a keyboard or mouse to support the wrist area during computer use.
wrist-rest.exampleUsage: The wrist rest sat in front of the keyboard.

monitor-stand.definition: A raised support that holds a computer monitor at a chosen height.
monitor-stand.exampleUsage: The monitor stand raised the screen slightly.

cable-organizer.definition: A clip, sleeve, tray, or other item used to keep cables arranged and reduce tangles.
cable-organizer.exampleUsage: The cable organizer kept the cords under the desk.

desk-calendar.definition: A calendar designed to stand or lie on a desk for quick reference.
desk-calendar.exampleUsage: The meeting date was marked on the desk calendar.

stamp.definition: A carved or raised object used to print the same design repeatedly.

shipping-label.definition: A label attached to a parcel showing delivery information, tracking codes, or handling details.
shipping-label.exampleUsage: The shipping label was attached to the top of the box.

packing-tape.definition: Strong adhesive tape used to seal cartons and packages.
packing-tape.exampleUsage: Packing tape sealed the shipping box.

bubble-wrap.definition: Plastic packing material with small air-filled bubbles that protects objects.

padded-envelope.definition: An envelope lined with cushioning material to protect its contents during delivery.
padded-envelope.exampleUsage: The small device was placed in a padded envelope.

return-label.definition: A shipping label supplied or generated so an item can be sent back to a seller or sender.
return-label.exampleUsage: The package included a return label.

postage-meter.definition: A device for large mailings that prints the required postage on each item and records the total amount charged.
postage-meter.exampleUsage: The clerk used the postage meter to apply the approved postage mark.

mail-slot.definition: An opening, usually built into a door, allows letters and other mail to be delivered.

letter-opener.definition: A small, blunt knife used to open envelopes or separate the uncut pages of books.
